# h2spec cases scripts/interop-http.sh expects to fail, one per line as
# <group>/<section>/<case>, exactly as the script prints them. The script
# runs the suite in clear text and behind TLS; an entry applies to both
# unless it starts with "clear:" or "tls:". Every entry names the RFC
# passage and the reason; an entry that starts passing fails the script so
# the list cannot go stale.
#
# h2spec v2.6.0 encodes RFC 7540. RFC 9113 obsoletes it: it dropped the
# self-dependency rule (5.3.1/1, 5.3.1/2) and the two "closed" cases below
# take the other branch of a MAY both texts offer (5.1/8, 5.1/9, 5.1/12).
# The preface case (3.5/2) is a design choice of this server — the preface
# is sniffed on a bare listener — that RFC 7540 and RFC 9113 word the same.

# RFC 9113 §3.4: an invalid preface is a connection error, and "a GOAWAY
# frame MAY be omitted in this case, since an invalid preface indicates
# that the peer is not using HTTP/2". Serve sniffs the preface on a bare
# listener (serve.go), so a stream that does not start with it is served
# as HTTP/1.1 and refused by that parser; h2spec reads the HTTP/1.1
# refusal as a truncated frame.
http2/3.5/2

# RFC 9113 §5.1, "closed": a peer that sent RST_STREAM and then sends on
# the stream has broken a MUST NOT, and the receiver "MAY treat receipt of
# any other type of frame on a closed stream as a connection error".
# RFC 7540 made the stream error mandatory; this server takes the other
# branch of the MAY and tolerates the frame for a while, because the
# RST_STREAM and the DATA may have crossed on the wire (h2conn.go, retire).
http2/5.1/8
http2/5.1/9

# RFC 9113 §5.1, "closed": same MAY. The cases close a stream by
# END_STREAM both ways and send DATA (5.1/11) or HEADERS (5.1/12) again;
# this server counts the DATA against the connection window, decodes the
# HEADERS block for the HPACK table, and drops either, sending nothing —
# §5.1 forbids any frame but PRIORITY on a closed stream — rather than the
# connection error RFC 7540 required (h2conn.go, data and reset; h2write.go,
# responded; TestH2NoResetOnAStreamClosedByBothEndStreams).
http2/5.1/11
http2/5.1/12

# RFC 9113 §5.3.2 deprecates the priority scheme and §6.2/§6.3 no longer
# say that a stream cannot depend on itself: the dependency fields are
# skipped, unread (h2conn.go, headers; frame, PRIORITY). ADR 0008 on
# the connection records that RFC 9218 is not implemented either.
http2/5.3.1/1
http2/5.3.1/2
